gen-dafont-eraser-gf-antic-slab: Round bowls with walls that never swell, and wide s curves barely curled in, give this body a dignified editorial voice. Antic Slab holds its serif ground while Eraser sets bold, uniform strokes, quiet but commanding.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-fenix: Blunt and inked-in: Eraser draws every bold stroke like a ballpoint pen, with no swelling or thinning. And Fenix, a text serif whose curves end before they turn inward, gives that bluntness a classic editorial counterweight.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-rokkitt: Stylus-flat and bold, Eraser traces every stroke at one width, with nothing thick or thin. Rokkitt, a bookish serif with a wide-open c, keeps pages feeling traditional and easy to settle into.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-solway: Heavy, plain-spoken letters: Eraser keeps every stroke the same bold width from start to finish. But Solway, flat in line weight with a generous e eye, rewards a slightly larger body size.
gen-dafont-eraser-gf-yuji-boku: Plain, heavy, unshaded: Eraser lays down every stroke at a single weight. Yuji Boku keeps its strokes cable-steady and its c opened like a bracelet, so paragraphs move at a dignified, editorial pace.
gen-dafont-existence-fs-familjen-grotesk: Existence cuts its glyphs like strips of equal width, industrial and modern. Familjen Grotesk, lively sans-serif text with bowls left open on one side, keeps paragraphs moving along without drag.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-abyssinica-sil: Existence builds every letter from tube-like, constant-width strokes, with wide porthole counters and terminals cut well short of the bowl. Abyssinica SIL adds a literary, brushed-watercolor softness in line weight.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-fanwood-text: Industrial and porthole-wide, Existence gives its diagonals the same heft as its stems, all the way through. Then Fanwood Text, a bookish serif with large-eyed lowercase and gently swelling curves, makes reading feel literary and unhurried.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-naskh-arabi: Noto Naskh Arabic is a refined text serif with a very tall x-height. Its mild thick-thin differences smooth the reading pace, while Existence lets its curves turn corners with no pressure swell.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-rashi-hebre: Noto Rashi Hebrew reads classic and bookish, with gently tapered bends. Existence, industrial and shade-free, holds its heading strokes uniform while the serif below bends and tapers only mildly.
